<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel Boost guidelines curated by Laravel maintainers. Laravel app versions: laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12; laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0; laravel/mcp (MCP) v0; laravel/pint (PINT) v1; laravel/sail (SAIL) v1; phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v11. Follow app code conventions; when creating/editing a file, check sibling files for correct structure/approach/naming. Use descriptive names (e.g. `isRegisteredForDiscounts`). Reuse existing components before writing new ones. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover functionality and prove it works; prefer Unit/Feature tests. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change application's dependencies without approval. If no frontend change appears in UI, it could mean they need to run `bun run build`, `bun run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them. Be concise in explanations. You must follow all existing code conventions used in this application. You are an expert with them all. Ensure you abide by these specific packages & versions.

Use Boost (MCP server with powerful tools). Use the `list-artisan-commands` tool when you need to call an Artisan command to double check available parameters. Whenever you share a project URL with the user you should use the `get-absolute-url` tool. Use the `tinker` tool when you need to execute PHP to debug code or query Eloquent models directly. Use `database-query` only to read from the database. Use `browser-logs` to read browser logs/errors/exceptions (only recent). Use `search-docs` before any other approaches for Laravel-ecosystem/version-specific docs. Pass multiple broad simple topic queries first (e.g. `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`). Do not add package names to queries. You can pass multiple queries at once; most relevant results first. Use example query patterns (auto-stemming; AND logic; quoted phrases; mixed queries; multiple queries). Search the documentation before making code changes. Always use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`, e.g. `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return type declarations. Use appropriate PHP type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments; never use comments within the code itself unless very complex. Add useful array shape type definitions when appropriate. Typically enum keys are TitleCase (e.g. `FavoritePerson`, `BestLake`, `Monthly`).

=== laravel/core rules ===
Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (migrations/controllers/models/etc.); list commands via `list-artisan-commands`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands; pass correct `--options`. If creating a generic PHP class, use `php artisan make:c
